merger_description:
The Independents Group, including the Independents Group Inc and The Independents Creative Collective UK Ltd (together, **TIG**), proposes to acquire 70% of the shares of five entities: Smuggler LLC, Division 7 LLC, Sidepiece LLC, Smuggler London Ltd and Smuggler Experience LLC (together, the **Smuggler Entities**) which form part of an international studio, marketing and production group (the **Smuggler Group**). As part of the acquisition, TIG (or one of its related entities) will also acquire a discretionary option to purchase the remaining 30% of shares in the Smuggler Entities, exercisable in 2030 (the **Acquisition**).

TIG is an international marketing communications services group mainly active in advertising, marketing, and communication activities.

Globally, the Smuggler Group is active in the production of audiovisual content. In Australia, Smuggler LLC produces audiovisual content for commercials and branded content.

determination_table_content.details:
The Independents Group, including the Independents Group Inc and
The Independents Creative Collective UK Ltd (together, TIG),
proposes to acquire 70% of the shares of five entities: Smuggler LLC,
Division 7 LLC, Sidepiece LLC, Smuggler London Ltd and Smuggler
Experience LLC (together, the Smuggler Entities) which form part of
an international studio, marketing and production group
(the Smuggler Group). As part of the acquisition, TIG (or one of its
related entities) will also acquire a discretionary option to purchase
the remaining 30% of shares in the Smuggler Entities, exercisable in
2030 (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, TIG, is an international marketing communications
services group mainly active in advertising, marketing, and
communication activities.
The target, the Smuggler Entities, are active globally in the
production of audiovisual content. In Australia, Smuggler LLC
produces audiovisual content for commercials and branded content.

The Parties overlap in the production and distribution of audiovisual
content.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and publicly available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• TIG (including its connected entities) and the Smuggler Entities
are not close competitors in the production of audiovisual
content in Australia. TIG primarily produces and distributes
audiovisual content for general entertainment, and the Smuggler
Entities produce short-form commercial and branded content for
advertisers and agencies.
• Both Parties have a very limited presence in Australia.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
